title: Smoothed health-probes + graceful connection-drain Terraform module for internal ALB/NLB
creator: Ava Patel
description: Add a reusable Terraform module that implements 'probe smoothing' and coordinated connection-draining behavior for internal ALB and NLB target groups. The goal is to reduce noisy flapping from transient probe failures during upgrades, autoscaling, and certificate rotation windows, and to ensure graceful de-registration so in-flight requests and long-lived streams complete. Module must support ALB target group deregistration_delay, NLB target group stickiness hints, configurable probe jitter/windowing, optional prober sidecar endpoint, and hooks for cert rotation canaries.
acceptance_criteria: New Terraform module (tf-module-ingress-drain) lives in infra/terraform/modules and exposes documented variables/outputs.
Module supports both ALB and NLB target group workflows via a single interface (provider switch variable).
Configurable probe smoothing parameters: consecutive_success_threshold, consecutive_failure_threshold, probe_jitter_ms, sliding_window_seconds.
Deregistration behavior aligns with provider: ALB deregistration_delay variable (default 300s) applied; NLB uses target health check grace + connection_tracking recommended values.
Module integrates optional prober sidecar selector (k8s) and a lightweight HTTP probe that emits smoothed health state when enabled.
End-to-end tests show a 60% reduction in transient failed health-state toggles during simulated rolling upgrades compared to baseline.
Documentation and example usage for: blue/green deploys, canary cert rotation, autoscaler induced scale-down, and on-prem private deployment patterns.
Peer-reviewed PR merged and Terraform fmt/tflint/terratest CI green.
Security review completed for prober sidecar (no privileged containers, minimal network scope).
implementation_notes: Primary module inputs: provider_type (alb|nlb), target_group_name, deregistration_delay_seconds, probe_path, probe_port, smoothing: {consecutive_success_threshold, consecutive_failure_threshold, probe_interval_seconds, probe_jitter_ms, sliding_window_seconds}, enable_prober_sidecar (bool), tls_termination_mode (edge|passthrough|internal), cert_rotation_hook (optional lambda/agent webhook URL)
Outputs: target_group_arn, prober_service_name (when enabled), health_policy_id, recommended_conn_drain_seconds

Key resources: aws_lb_target_group (ALB/NLB variations), aws_lb_target_group_attachment, aws_lb_target_group_health_check, null_resource to render prober config for k8s, aws_lb_listener_rule helper for TLS termination knobs.

Health smoothing algorithm: sliding window with exponential backoff jitter to avoid synchronized probe storms across replicas. Implementation uses local-exec to generate a JSON config for the prober sidecar and a simple Helm values snippet for examples.

For ALB: set deregistration_delay to module.deregistration_delay_seconds and ensure target group health check interval <= probe interval. For NLB: recommend enabling proxy protocol or use connection_tracking tuning in host kernel as noted in README.

Cert rotation flow: module provides cert_rotation_hook variable (URL) which will be called pre-rotate; the hook should trigger a canary group where smoothing is temporarily relaxed to speed failover tests.
Backward compat: add migration notes for services using older tf modules (mapping table for variable names).
testing_plan: Unit: tflint, terraform validate, and module-level terragrunt runs in CI.

Integration: terratest suite spins up a small VPC with ALB + autoscaling group (3 instances) and runs rolling upgrade scenarios while injecting transient probe failures (tcp-reset, 500s). Verify health-state stability metrics.
Performance: measure probe-induced CPU on prober sidecar at 1000 endpoints/region simulation.
Chaos: k8s pod kill storms during drain window to validate no request loss for in-flight connections (synth load generator).
Security: container image scan for prober sidecar, network policy tests to ensure prober cannot reach control plane resources by default.
Canary deploy: deploy module to a single customer-like environment and run certificate rotation canary before global rollout.
Automated assertions: reduce flapping events by >=60% and target deregistration compliance (no active connections dropped) in 95th percentile of runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module into infra repo as experimental (feature flag).
2) Deploy to staging VPC and run terratest suite (green required).
3) Create a canary service using the module for one non-critical customer/private deployment. Monitor for 48-72 hours.
4) Gradually enable for internal critical services (console, internal-gateway) with 2-hour maintenance windows and rollback playbook available.
5) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry, flip default enable_prober_sidecar to true in templates and announce migration plan.
6) Document migration checklist and migration tf state helpers.
risks: Prober sidecar may add resource overhead; need strict default limits and optional disable flag.
Incorrect smoothing settings could delay detection of real failures (operational risk). Mitigation: conservative defaults + visible metrics.
Deregistration_delay misconfiguration may increase warmup/coldstart windows for scaling down (cost impact).
Cross-account or multi-AZ NLB nuances (connection-tracking) could behave differently on prem than cloud provider; add platform-specific guides.
Certificate rotation canaries if miswired could leave targets in degraded state; provide explicit dry-run mode.
